0.original: G'raha Tia is ready to set forth.

48.original: Considering the Omicrons' single-minded character, the lack of new orders does seem unusual. I agree that we should seek out their leader.

49.original: “Pointless exercise”... What does that mean, I wonder...

50.original: So, the console we seek lies on the far side of this isle.

51.original: Given the nature of the ground, the route may not be entirely direct as it seems.

52.original: Let us all watch our step as we make our way.

53.original: The glow would suggest it is still operational. But how are we to interact with it...?

54.original: Greetings, Sir! Can you hear me? Say something if you can! Awaken! Activate! ...Password!

56.original: This appears to be the console.

58.original: Would you care to take a look at it?

59.original: Judging by the size of the Omicrons we've met, I'm reasonably confident the console is controlled via the orb.

60.original: You try touching, smacking, and attuning with the console, but there is no response...

62.original: But there must be a way to activate it. There must...

63.original: I remember when we set Omega loose to deal with Shinryu...

64.original: An Allagan weapon, we once thought. And here we are now, visiting a recreation of its home world.

65.original: I can only imagine how else these beings will surprise us...

66.original: Though I never encountered Omega myself, in conceiving the means to send the Crystal Tower to the First, we borrowed much from its mastery of the rift.

67.original: Indeed, so many times did I read the report of your battle, I believe I could recite it word for word.

68.original: Omega's miniature likeness also survived to the future, if a little worse for the wear. I must confess, I was delighted to see it again in the present.

69.original: Though I never encountered Omega myself, in conceiving the means to send the Crystal Tower to the First, we derived no small inspiration from its abilities.

70.original: In the course of my research, I devoured every single piece of literature I could find on the being. To think that the knowledge would prove useful here, at the edge of existence...

71.original: Let us focus our search on the outpost.

72.original: Alisaie and I will try speaking with the Omicrons this time, in the hopes we might learn something new.

73.original: Meanwhile, perhaps you and G'raha could observe them from a distance.

74.original: These beings are systematic and routine by nature. If there are any that aren't, it shouldn't be too difficult to spot them.

75.original: If there are no questions, then let us begin at once!

76.original: As we came this way, I believe I spied a promising vantage point. Follow me.

77.original: We will be certain to ask about the extended operations unit.

78.original: Not only do they look the same; they say the same things as well...

79.original: And here we are. I see the twins are wasting no time with their inquiries.

80.original: Let us begin observing the Omicrons. They are supposed to be standing by, so we should look for any that aren't.

81.original: Search Base Omicron for errant Omicrons. You may move the camera, as well as zoom in and out. Target an Omicron and examine it with <hex:020825E4E95101FF10024804F2022203EE81910248020103FF0E021E021003202F20021E02090303>.

84.original: It's left the base. Let's follow it!

85.original: It's not here, but it definitely came this way. It must have used the portal.

86.original: Time to go through and see what we find...

87.original: Nothing nearby save malfunctioning units. Come─the portal awaits.

93.original: Quite an unusual specimen... What is the device attached to it?

94.original: The tree is a sample collected from another star. As it cannot survive in our environment, however, it requires life support. That is the function of the device.

95.original: To go to such lengths to sustain it... Is there something special about this tree?

96.original: Being foreign matter, protocol requires that we study it. As this task has been completed, the specimen may be discarded.

97.original: However, when I behold the tree, I am made to feel as though...there is a problem.

98.original: In order to become strong, we have continued to enhance ourselves. Like we did countless others, we conquered the star whence this tree came.

99.original: It is the last remnant of a dead world, and there is nothing towards which it may aspire. Yet it grows. Extends its branches. Sprouts leaves. Produces seeds.

100.original: Why does it seek to continue?

101.original: Why was it made to behave in such a way, and to what end? I do not understand.

102.original: ...I see. Out of curiosity, does this pertain to your duty?

103.original: ...No, it does not. My apologies, I shall return to my designated post and assume a state of combat readiness.

104.original: So, it was acting outside of orders...

105.original: Perhaps it is simply a malfunctioning Omicron. These are by no means uncommon.

106.original: But it may also be a unit possessed of the ability to make decisions. One not unlike Sir...

107.original: I believe this bears further investigation.

108.original: To endeavor to live even if we must depend on forces beyond our control...

109.original: Tell me, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. One day, when this adventure becomes a part of your epic, do you think I will be mentioned in it?

111.original: Of course. Why wouldn't you be?

113.original: You're not here so you can be in a story.

114.original: You truly think so? That would be a...

115.original: Nay, I shouldn't say such things until the moment comes to pass. Never mind the embarrassment...

116.original: Oh, come now, how much would it have cost you to simply nod?

117.original: 'Tis no simple thing to earn a place beside you, this I know full well. But it is something to hope for as I forge on.

118.original: ...Forgive me. Let there be no doubt that fame and glory could not be further from my mind.

119.original: And yet...I would be lying if I said that I don't relish the thought of my name being spoken in the same breath as yours.

120.original: ...Well, we had best get on with our task.

121.original: Tracking down Sir, and understanding the nature of the emotion which bars our way!
